content:
From angle-as-turn to Euler's formula, Understanding Elementary Shapes is the widest chapter of Class 6 geometry — triangles, quadrilaterals, polygons and 3-D solids in one sweep. Here is what the Olympiad asks, the classifications to memorise, and a free 10-question test with figures.

What the Class 6 Maths Olympiad Understanding Elementary Shapes chapter tests

  • Angles as revolutions; clock-hand angles
  • Triangles by sides and by angles
  • Quadrilateral family: square, rectangle, parallelogram, rhombus, trapezium
  • 3-D solids, faces-edges-vertices and Euler's formula

Key facts your child should know

  • One revolution = 360°; each clock hour mark = 30°.
  • Triangle angles total 180° — at most one right or obtuse angle.
  • A rhombus has equal sides; a rectangle equal angles; a square both.
  • Euler's formula: F + V − E = 2 — a cube: 6 + 8 − 12 = 2.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Calling every four-sided equal-length figure a square (a rhombus need not have right angles).
  • Saying a triangle can have two right angles.
  • Counting a cylinder's edges as straight edges.

faq.q: What angle do clock hands make at 3 o'clock?
faq.a: 90° — each hour mark is 30°, and 3 marks × 30° = 90°.
For any polyhedron, Faces + Vertices − Edges = 2. A cube: 6 + 8 − 12 = 2.
